Metadata.CommitMsg:
feat(infra): parametriza portas do compose para worktrees paralelos (#110)

* feat(infra): parametriza portas do compose para worktrees paralelos

Permite rodar varios worktrees do mesmo repo em paralelo com 'docker
compose up' sem colisao de portas no host. As portas internas dos
containers nao mudam; defaults (8000/5432/8080) sao retro-compativeis.

- docker-compose.yml: ${APP_PORT}, ${DB_PORT}, ${UI_PORT} com defaults
- .env.dev.example: comenta os 3 vars + BACKEND_URL para slot custom
- Makefile (reset-db): poll do health-check e echo final usam APP_PORT/UI_PORT
- docs/setup/worktrees-paralelos.md: guia com tabela de slots sugerida

* fix(infra): docker compose --env-file .env.dev no Makefile para .env.dev controlar portas

Vulnerabilities.Title: NiceGUI has a path traversal in app.add_media_files() allows arbitrary file read
Vulnerabilities.Description: NiceGUI is a Python-based UI framework. Versions 3.3.1 and below are vulnerable to  directory traversal through the App.add_media_files() function, which allows a remote attacker to read arbitrary files on the server filesystem. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: NiceGUI apps which use `ui.sub_pages` vulnerable to zero-click XSS
Vulnerabilities.Description: NiceGUI is a Python-based UI framework. From versions 2.22.0 to 3.4.1, an unsafe implementation in the pushstate event listener used by ui.sub_pages allows an attacker to manipulate the fragment identifier of the URL, which they can do despite being cross-site, using an iframe. This issue has been patched in version 3.5.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: NiceGUI's Path Traversal via Unsanitized FileUpload.name Enables Arbitrary File Write
Vulnerabilities.Description: NiceGUI is a Python-based UI framework. Prior to 3.7.0, NiceGUI's FileUpload.name property exposes client-supplied filename metadata without sanitization, enabling path traversal when developers use the pattern UPLOAD_DIR / file.name. Malicious filenames containing ../ sequences allow attackers to write files outside intended directories, with potential for remote code execution through application file overwrites in vulnerable deployment patterns. This design creates a prevalent security footgun affecting applications following common community patterns. Note: Exploitation requires application code incorporating file.name into filesystem paths without sanitization. Applications using fixed paths, generated filenames, or explicit sanitization are not affected. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.7.0.
